question.text: Sunita, a government employee, retires and receives leave encashment of Rs.28,00,000. Separately, a private sector employee Pooja also retires and receives leave encashment of Rs.28,00,000. What is the exempt amount for each?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10(10AA) of the Income Tax Act exempts leave encashment received on retirement, but the treatment differs by employer type. For Central/State Government employees, the entire amount received as leave encashment on retirement is fully exempt with no monetary ceiling. For non-Government (private-sector) employees, the exemption is the least of (a) actual leave encashment, (b) ten months' average salary, (c) a salary-based computation, or (d) a notified monetary cap — currently Rs.25,00,000. So Sunita's Rs.28,00,000 is fully exempt; Pooja's exemption is capped at Rs.25,00,000, leaving Rs.3,00,000 taxable. The Trap: Applying Rs.25,00,000 to both ignores the full exemption available to government employees. Treating both as fully exempt ignores the private-sector cap. The "Rs.25,00,000 / Rs.3,00,000" option misreads the question — Sunita keeps the full Rs.28,00,000 exemption, not Rs.25,00,000. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages reviewed in the audit include leave encashment in salary and list Section 10(10AA) Leave Salary as exempt, but the specific government-employee full exemption, the non-government Rs.25,00,000 cap, and the resulting exemption amounts are not on the pages checked. The framing above reflects the standard Section 10(10AA) treatment under the Income Tax Act.
